{{Quote|In the light, there is a darkness and in the darkness, a light. It is the way with us all. Be a prisoner of neither Bogan nor Ashla. Strive to live in balance. As Tython itself teaches us, it is dangerous to do otherwise. And the danger is there&mdash;always.|[[Ketu]]|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
The '''Je'daii Order''' was an ancient organization unified by its belief and observance of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] on the planet [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. Focusing on maintaining a balance in the Force, a state to which Tython was itself hospitable, the Je'daii saw the Force as two aspects of a whole; the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|Ashla]] (Light) and the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Bogan]] (Dark). They saw this duality in the Force represented in the night sky of Tython in the form of two [[Moon/Legends|moons]]; one named [[Ashla (moon)/Legends|Ashla]] and bathed in light, the other named [[Bogan]] and shrouded in darkness. In keeping with their view of balance, Je'daii who fell too far to either the light or dark were exiled to the opposite respective moon to [[Meditation/Legends|meditate]] until they returned to balance.

The Order's presence on Tython was distributed between nine Temples, each of which was presided over by a [[Je'daii Temple Master]]. In order to gain [[Je'daii Master|mastery]] in the Order, all Je'daii were expected to travel to each of the Temples to hone different skills. The Order was led by a [[Je'daii Council|Council of Masters]], consisting of the nine Temple Masters, which decided important matters and directed the Order. Surviving on Tython for millennia in isolation from the rest of the galaxy, the Order was deeply shaken by the arrival of a [[Force Hound]] from the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].

In the years following the Hound's initial crash landing on Tython, a schism shook the Order to its foundation. After a [[Force Wars|bloody civil war]], known to history as the first conflict between light and dark side philosophies, the dark side adherents were routed while the Jedi Order thrived. A large group of Jedi departed Tython, eventually finding a new home on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], where they would eventually join the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] as defenders of the peace.

==History==
===Early history===
{{Quote|Observing the world around them, they saw two moons in the one sky&mdash;light Ashla and dark Bogan&mdash;and they understood the dual aspects to the Force, light and dark. The light defined the dark as the dark did the light. When balance was not maintained, Tython reacted to the imbalance with severe storms and quakes. And so the travelers defined themselves, ever seeking a balance. They became the Je'daii, a Dai Bendu term meaning "''mystic center.''" Only through the harmony of balance could the Je'daii maintain a peaceful world.|Ketu|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
[[File:Tho_Yor_Arrival.png|thumb|left|300px|The Tho Yor Arrival]]
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[36,453 BBY]], the [[Tho Yor]]&mdash;eight great pyramid [[Starship/Legends|ships]] that were scattered across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]&mdash;called out to the inhabitants of the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] they were located on, including [[Ando Prime/Legends|Ando Prime]], [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]], [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], and [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. Through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the Tho Yor convinced the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] around them to board the starships, and the pyramid ships then departed the planets upon which they had sat for so long and set out into the galaxy. The Tho Yor then traveled the galaxy, gathering Force-sensitives of many other [[Species/Legends|species]], so that by the [[Time/Legends|time]] the eight ships journeyed into the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] together, they carried members of the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]], [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]], [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]], [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]], [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]], [[Cathar/Legends|Cathar]], [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]], [[Noghri/Legends|Noghri]], [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], [[Talid/Legends|Talid]], [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]], [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]], [[Human/Legends|Human]],<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]],<ref name="DOTJ 2">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 2]]</ref> and [[Krevaaki]] species,<ref name="Into the Void" /> as well as the [[Koorivar/Legends|species later known as the Koorivar]].<ref name="DOTJ 8">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 3]]</ref> The eight Tho Yor traveled into the Deep Core to the planet [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], where a ninth and far larger Tho Yor awaited them as it floated above a pinnacle of stone. The arrival of the Tho Yor was heralded by an immense [[Force_Storm_(Tython)|Force Storm]] that swept over the entire planet, and the eight Tho Yor first gathered around the ninth Tho Yor before scattering themselves across the planet.<ref name="DOTJ 1" />

The [[Tho Yor Arrival]], as the event came to be known,<ref name="Into the Void" /> saw each Tho Yor deposit their passengers at their final destination and remain there, with some of the ships burying themselves in the landscape while others remained floating in the sky. The Force-sensitive pilgrims immediately realized that Tython was uniquely strong in the Force, and the pilgrims&mdash;known collectively as the [[Tythan]]s&mdash;soon realized that they had been brought to Tython in order to study the Force and to learn to control and master the abilities it granted them. However, Tython's beauty came with dangers, and the pilgrims' lives became a constant form of moving meditation on the Force, rather than sitting in silent meditation. The pilgrims also realized that Tython itself reacted violently with Force Storms and quakes to imbalance between the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark sides]] of the Force, which they named Ashla and Bogan after Tython's two [[Moon/Legends|moons]]: the bright satellite [[Ashla (moon)/Legends|Ashla]], and the dark moon of [[Bogan]]. The pilgrims therefore formed the Je'daii Order, taking their name from the [[Dai Bendu language|language]] of the [[Order of Dai Bendu|Dai Bendu]] monks of the Talid species: combining the words ''je'', meaning mystic, and ''dai'', meaning center.<ref name="DOTJ 1" />

The philosophy of the Balance became essential to survival on Tython, as harmony and balance between Ashla and Bogan maintained the peaceful beauty of Tython and prevented the chaos and destruction that came with imbalance. Over the next thousand years, the Je'daii built the [[Je'daii Temples]], [[City/Legends|cities]] and centers of learning and healing that each centered around one of the Tho Yor.<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> [[Padawan Kesh]], the Je'daii academy, was established by the year [[36,019 BBY]], when [[Nordia Gral]] was serving as Padawan Kesh's first [[Je'daii Temple Master|Temple Master]]. Around that time, Master Gral helped develop the tradition of the [[Great Journey]], a pilgrimage across Tython to each of the Temples that all Je'daii would take upon graduating from the rank of [[Padawan (Je'daii)|Padawan]] to [[Je'daii Journeyer|Journeyer]].<ref name="Into the Void" /> However, as the years passed, the Je'daii began to have children who were not Force-sensitive, and it eventually became clear to the Tythans that the planet was not safe for those who could not touch the Force after the city of [[Aurum]] was destroyed. Therefore, during the second millennium after the Tho Yor Arrival, a [[second migration]] occurred: all Tythans who were not Force-sensitive were made to leave the planet, even if it broke up families, and the non-Force-sensitives settled first on Ashla and Bogan before spreading out to the other worlds of the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]].<ref name="DOTJ 1" />

===Era of peace===
Despite the services the Order provided to the other Settled Worlds, the existence of the Je'daii on their isolated world of Tython became a thing of legend. It wasn't until the reign of [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Hadiya]] of [[Shikaakwa]] that a full-blown conflict erupted between the Order and the non-Force-sensitives that shared the star system. In a system-wide conflict known as the [[Despot War]], Queen Hadiya led her [[Despot Army|army]] against Tython in a series of campaigns in [[25,805 BBY]]. Despite massive casualties on both sides, the Je'daii Order was able to vanquish Hadiya and her forces and return the balance to Tython. While balance was indeed restored, turmoil festered on Tython just [[25,793 BBY|twelve years later]] when the Je'daii Order found the wreckage of the first ship to enter the system since the Tho Yor brought their ancestors to the world. The [[Rakatan ship|ship]], of [[Infinite Empire/Legends|unknown]] origin, crashed on Tython in area known as the [[Rift]], close to the Temple of [[Anil Kesh]], and the mass deaths sparked a Force storm of proportions not seen since the arrival of the Tho Yor. Representatives of the Order investigated the crash site and encountered a sole survivor: a [[Force Hound|mysterious man]] named [[Tau (individual)|Xesh]] who carried a bizarre weapon known as a [[Forcesaber]].<ref name="DOTJ 2" />

In [[25,793 BBY]], the forces of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] invaded the Tython system. [[Skal'nas]] sought to reverse his [[Species/Legends|species's]] gradual loss of control over the Force by acquiring the [[Infinity Gate]] said to exist on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Tython, and his forces [[Attack on Fury Station|attacked]] the [[Space station/Legends|space station]] [[Fury Station]] on the edges of the system before [[Capture of Obri|capturing]] [[Capture of Mawr|both]] of the gas giants [[Obri]] and [[Mawr]]. The Rakata and their [[Flesh Raider]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] [[First battle of Tython|attacked]] Tython, but were repelled by the Je'daii Order; the Infinite Empire fell back to the forest world of [[Ska Gora]] and [[Fall of Ska Gora|conquered]] it before establishing their [[Rakatan Base Prime|main command post]] there. By the end of the first year, the Je'daii had allied themselves with the forces of the [[Settled Worlds]], placing Je'daii Master [[Rajivari]] in command of the joint forces. The Order also constructed Forcesabers, the Dark side weapons of the Rakata, and armed themselves with the weapons as they recalled the insane [[Daegen Lok]] to lead them in battle as Lok had foreseen.

===The Force Wars===
{{Main|Force Wars}}
[[File:Force_Wars-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The [[Force Wars]] of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]].]]
In the ensuing decade,<ref name="Timeline" /> the balance of the Je'daii Order was shattered. Two splinter groups emerged, one which held the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|Ashla]] as the main power of good in the universe, and another whose members found power only in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Bogan]]. In a tumultuous conflict known as the [[Force Wars]], former allies were pitted against each other and all that the Je'daii Order had become was torn asunder.<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

In [[25,783 BBY]] the war had raged for nearly a decade, leaving the planet a ruined waste.<ref name="Timeline" /> The light-siders, led by [[Je'daii Master]]s [[Rajivari]], [[Garon Jard]], [[Cala Brin]] and [[Ters Sendon]], founded a new group known as the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and deemed that they would only use their powers for the protection of the weak and disenfranchised. From this group, Master Rajivari broke away and formed a dissident group of dark siders. Rajivari and his followers seized the Temple of [[Kaleth]] and attempted to defeat the Jedi Order. Following the defeat of Rajivari's forces<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> and other dissidents like him, the Je'daii Order was finished, the Jedi Order standing in its place. Having witnessed the destructive power of the dark side first hand with the ruination of their homeworld, a large group of Jedi set out from Tython to settle other worlds far from the Deep Core, eventually establishing a headquarters on the far-flung world [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]].<ref name="NEC" />

The Je'daii's successor group, the Jedi would ultimately go on to defend the galaxy for millennia to come.<ref name="NEC" /> The [[Bendu symbol]] inspired the [[Republic crest/Legends|Republic crest]] used by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]&mdash;the Republic's successor state&mdash;instituted a six-spoked [[Imperial crest/Legends|Imperial crest]] reminiscent of the Bendu symbol.<ref name="CCS">''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

By [[36 ABY]], the [[Historical Council]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] had learned that the Jedi Order had been founded on Tython following the Force Wars, but didn't know that there had previously been an order that sought to maintain balance between the Ashla and the Bogan.<ref name="NEC" />

==Organization==
===Structure===
{{Quote|Those born with an affinity to the Force were always brought back to Tython. From youngling to apprentice, from Journeyer to Ranger, and finally to Master, a Je'daii grew. Passing from one temple to another, seeking knowledge, seeking balance in the Force&mdash;their creed a message of peace.|Ketu|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
[[File:JedaiiCouncil-ForceStorm4.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Members of the Je'daii Council meet in conference.]]
A monastic order of scientists, scholars, warriors, philosophers, and artisans that were the sole inhabitants of the planet Tython, the Je'daii Order<ref name="DOTJ 0" /> was governed by the Je'daii Council,<ref name="Into the Void" /> also known as the Masters' Council<ref name="DOTJ 2" /> or the Council of Masters.<ref name="Into the Void" /> The Council was composed of the nine Je'daii Temple Masters, the highest rank a Je'daii could achieve in the Order, who each oversaw one of the nine Temples that were scattered across Tython. Though there were nine Je'daii Temples, the actual number of Temple Masters occasionally varied from nine; a mated [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]] couple named [[Calleh]] and [[Naro]] jointly held the position of Temple Master at Mahara Kesh, the Temple of Healing.<ref name="DOTJ 0" /> The Je'daii Council met in [[Hologram/Legends|holoconference]]<ref name="DOTJ 4" /> or in person at Kaleth,<ref name="DOTJ 0" /> and the Council had the authority to exile Je'daii to the moons of Ashla or Bogan if they strayed too close to one side of the Force.<ref name="DOTJ 6">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 1]]</ref>

After the departure of all non-Force-sensitives from Tython, it became customary for any Force-sensitives who were born on the other worlds to be sent to Tython, where they were trained as Je'daii. Any non-Force-sensitives who were born on Tython were tested to see if they possessed any aptitude for the Force, but if not, they were asked to leave the world, as it was unsafe for those who could not touch the Force.<ref name="Into the Void" /> Young Force-sensitive [[Je'daii initiate]]s were trained and housed at Padawan Kesh until they were taken on as a Padawan by a Je'daii Master.<ref name="DOTJ 0" /> Once a Padawan's training was complete, normally when the Padawan was in their teens, they were made [[Je'daii Journeyer]]s and sent on their Great Journey: an odyssey across the surface of Tython to visit each of the Temples. Great Journeys typically lasted two years, and Journeyers would trek unaccompanied and largely by foot across Tython to reach each of the Temples, where they would spend several weeks learnings the skills taught at each Temple. Most Journeyers chose a discipline to specialize in during their Great Journey, and many returned to the Temple that taught that discipline later in life as Rangers or Masters.<ref name="Into the Void" />

If the Journeyer survived, upon the successful completion of their Great Journey they were elevated to the rank of Je'daii Ranger. Rangers were deployed by the Je'daii Council all across the Tython system, fulfilling assignments and missions requested by the Council or the other Settled Worlds. Rangers wore a badge known as a [[Ranger star]] to signify their rank, and they were given their choice of a starship: either a [[Hunter-class starfighter|''Hunter''-class starfighter]], or the larger [[Peacemaker-class cruiser|''Peacemaker''-class cruiser]]. Rangers were tasked with missions of diplomacy, tracking fugitives, ending conflicts, and a wide variety of other missions, and some Rangers rarely returned to Tython. If a Je'daii Ranger had shown sufficient experience, wisdom, and understanding of the Force, they might be promoted to the rank of [[Je'daii Master]], which was the highest rank a Je'daii could achieve other than a Temple Master. Numerous Masters made their home at each Temple, providing their knowledge to younger Je'daii and studying the Force and other pursuits.<ref name="Into the Void" />

===The Temples===
{{Quote|As the millennium unfolded, the Je'daii built a great civilization, establishing temples, cities, seats of learning and healing, each centered around a Tho Yor.|Ketu|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
[[File:Training_at_Stav.png|thumb|left|300px|Je'daii training at Stav Kesh.]]
Early in the Je'daii Order's history, the Order established their nine Je'daii Temples around the nine Tho Yor across Tython. While other cities and settlements were later built, the nine Temples were home to most of the planet's inhabitants and were the seats of the Order's presence upon Tython. [[Akar Kesh]], the Temple of Balance, was considered to be one of the most sacred Temples, and it was built within the great pinnacle of stone above which the largest Tho Yor hovered. The Temple of Science, [[Anil Kesh]], straddled the planetary rift known as the [[Chasm]] near its floating Tho Yor, and its inhabitants meddled in science and [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemy]]. The Temple of Healing, Mahara Kesh, was located in the [[Deep Ocean]], and the Temple of the Arts, [[Bodhi]],<ref name="DOTJ 0" /> was located on the plains of the continent [[Masara]].<ref name="Into the Void" />

Padawan Kesh housed and trained young Je'daii before they became Padawans, while the Temple of Martial Arts, [[Stav Kesh]], was located high in the [[Ice Giant Range]] next to the Tho Yor that had buried itself in the mountains. [[Vur Tepe]]&mdash;the Forge&mdash;was located directly over an active volcano near its floating Tho Yor, and its inhabitants focused themselves on the creation of weapons and anything else that Anil Kesh's scientists could think of. The Temple of Force Skills, Qigong Kesh, was located in an enormous cavern beneath its floating Tho Yor in Tython's [[Silent Desert]], and the last Temple&mdash;Kaleth, the Temple of Knowledge&mdash;was home to the Je'daii Library and the meeting place for the entire Order.<ref name="DOTJ 0" />

==Philosophy==
{{Quote|Not necessarily, Harun. Hate is understandable, as is anger. Anger has its uses. It cleanse like fire. But one must never only feel hate or only feel anger. That brings one out of balance.|[[Ketu|Master Ketu]] to [[Harun]] and [[Resi]]|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
[[File:TythonBoganAshla-DotJ0.png|thumb|right|300px|Tython's moons, Ashla and Bogan, inspired the Je'daii philosophy of the Balance.]]
The Je'daii Order's primarily philosophy was that of the Balance&mdash;because of Tython's intense reactions to imbalance in the Force, the Je'daii strived to maintain personal balance between the light and dark sides of the Force. This philosophy was also inspired by Tython's moons: bright Ashla represented the light side of the Force, and the dark moon Bogan represented the dark side.<ref name="DOTJ 0" /> In Je'daii philosophy, they acknowledged the fact that there was always a light within darkness, and darkness within light, so that it was impossible for one to ever be truly free of either.<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> Unlike the later Jedi Order, Je'daii were encouraged to give into the temptations of both the light and the dark, as they believed it was necessary to embrace both in order to learn more about the Force.<ref name="DOTJ 7">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 2]]</ref> Nevertheless, the Je'daii were careful to keep their emotions under control and discouraged exclusively using the dark side.<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> The Je'daii viewed living on Tython as a near-constant meditation and study of the Force, and the Great Journey was intended to expose young Journeyers to the various disciplines and arts that were studied at each temple.<ref name="Into the Void" />

===Code===
{{Quote|There is no ignorance; there is knowledge.<br />There is no fear; there is power.<br />I am the heart of the Force.<br />I am the revealing fire of light.<br />I am the mystery of darkness<br />In balance with chaos and harmony,<br />Immortal in the Force.|The Je'daii Code|<ref name="DOTJ 0" />}}
The Je'daii Order developed their own [[Je'daii Code|code]], which illustrated the primary tenets of the Order's philosophy, and was taught at all of the Temples across Tython. Because of Tython's proclivity for Force Storms, the Je'daii took it upon themselves to police their ranks for those who fell out of balance, and they exiled those who were out of balance to Tython's moons. Those who delved too deep into the dark side were exiled to Bogan, where they were instructed to meditate on the light side and the bright moon of Ashla. On the other hand, those Je'daii who clung to the light side over the Balance were sent to Ashla, where they meditated on the darkness of the moon Bogan to bring themselves back into balance.<ref name="DOTJ 0" /> Exiles on Tython's moons received regular deliveries of [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]], and they were kept separate from other exiles by their cuffs and the sentry droids that patrolled the moons.<ref name="DOTJ 6" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Je'daii don't see a division of the light and dark side; instead, they believe a balance is necessary between the two. The Je'daii are like the Titans in Greek mythology who came before the gods. They are beings of great power and ability, but not all-knowing. They struggle with the idea of balance in the Force and know that being out of balance affects their power and the planet Tython itself.|John Ostrander|<ref name="CBR">{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/nycc-exclusive-ostrander-and-duursema-unveil-star-wars-dawn-of-the-jedi|text=NYCC EXCLUSIVE: Ostrander and Duursema Unveil "Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi"|archivedate=20200817183352|author=Shaun Manning|date=2011-10-13}}</ref>}}
The planet Tython and the possibility that the Force was discovered on it were first mentioned in ''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''. However, ''Power of the Jedi Sourcebook'' exclusively mentioned worship of the Ashla on Tython.<ref name="POTJ">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' mentioned that there was a rivalry between Ashla and Bogan followers on Tython that lead to the Force Wars and the formation of the Jedi Order, but made no mention of anyone using both the Ashla and the Bogan or of any order preceding the Jedi Order.<ref name="NEC" /> When [[John Ostrander]] announced ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi]]'', he revealed the existence of the Je'daii Order.<ref name="CBR" />
